subject: Processing locations and cross-border transfer pathways for ClearWater Health
messages:
From: Amanda Chen <amanda@clearwaterhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwaterhealth.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency and cross-border routing questions

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — ClearWater Health is interested but our security team needs clarity on where customer data is processed and whether any PII could cross borders. Two specific asks:

1) For requests that come from our US application, can processing be restricted to US regions only (no transfers to EU/APAC)?
2) We need an inventory of subprocessors that may access logs or telemetry (even if just for ops).

Procurement also wants to see a template DPA clause that guarantees region pinning and deletion timelines. Can you share details and any existing artifacts?

— Amanda

-----Original Message-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amanda Chen <amanda@clearwaterhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@clearwaterhealth.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 13:02:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency and cross-border routing questions

Hi Amanda — thanks for the clear list. High level reply up front: yes, we support region pinning for request processing and persistent storage, and we can provide a subprocessors inventory and a DPA clause template.

Details below, and I attached the Security Appendix and a CSV export of our current region/subprocessor mapping for you to share with your team. If you want formal attestation (SOC2 Type II excerpt) we can route that through our security portal as a next step.

Short answers:
- Processing: For Hosted API traffic we primarily process requests in the nearest available Redwood-hosted region by default. ClearWater can request region pinning to any supported region (e.g., us-west-2, us-east-1) — pinned requests will be routed and executed only in the pinned region(s).
- Storage & logs: Customer prompt/response artifacts are stored in the region you select for your workspace. Operational logs are aggregated for monitoring in a separate telemetry layer; access to telemetry is limited and covered by subprocessors and contracts.
- Cross-border fallback: We have automated fallback rules when pinned capacity is exhausted. Fallback is disabled by default for customers who require strict residency; enabling fallback may route to a geographically proximate region within the same jurisdiction if you permit it.

I'm summarizing the endpoints and subprocessors below — Monica, Priyom, I left some open items for you to confirm:

1) Primary processing hosts (examples):
   - AWS us-west-2 (Redwood-managed instances) — inference runtime
   - GCP us-central1 (partner pool) — dedicated capacity option
   - Azure eastus (partner pool) — only used for Dedicated customers on request

2) Subprocessors with potential access to telemetry/aggregated logs:
   - LogStore Inc. (log ingestion and short-term retention)
   - FastPath CDN (edge caching for static assets) — does not see raw prompts
   - Nimbus Infra (hardware partner for Dedicated pools) — under NDA and limited access

3) Data transfer model:
   - Request processing and KV cache are kept in-region when pinned.
   - Long-term analytics (aggregated, pseudonymized metrics) may be replicated to our analytics region (us-east-1) for multi-customer dashboards unless you opt-out via contract.

Next steps: I can provide a DPA clause and a checkbox in the console to disable fallback. Monica — can you confirm the telemetry retention window and the exact subprocessors list? Priyom — can you confirm whether region pinning is available for Dedicated and Private deployments the same way as Hosted?

Best,
Marcus

-----Original Message-----
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amanda Chen <amanda@clearwaterhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@clearwaterhealth.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 14:10:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency and cross-border routing questions

Hi Amanda,

Thanks for flagging the requirements. A few clarifications from Security:

- Telemetry & operational logs: we retain operational telemetry for 90 days by default (metrics/traces/alerts). Aggregate diagnostics for product improvement are retained up to 2 years but are pseudonymized and cannot be used to reconstruct customer prompts.
- Subprocessors: the attached CSV lists all subprocessors as of 2026-05-01. Notable entries: LogStore Inc. (access limited to ingestion API), FastPath CDN (edge node metadata only), and AuditVault (retention vault for audit logs). We run periodic vendor reviews and can provide SOC2 exhibits for the bigger partners.
- Deletion: customers can request dataset deletion; on Hosted we perform deletion from primary stores within 30 days and from analytics/pseudonymized stores within 90 days. For Dedicated/Private, deletion timelines are configurable in the contract.

For strict residency, set workspace region to your desired AWS region and check the "Disable cross-region fallback" option. That ensures generation, KV cache, and primary storage remain in-region; it does not prevent your users from sending requests that originate from other countries (network egress is separate).

If you want, I can produce a concise one-page summary for your legal team that includes the subprocessors list, retention/deletion timelines, and the DPA clause we usually use.

— Monica Patel
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amanda Chen <amanda@clearwaterhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwaterhealth.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency and cross-border routing questions

Hi Amanda — quick privacy note: region pinning is supported in Hosted (workspace-level) and in Dedicated (cluster-level). For Private deployments you control the entire network stack and there is no Redwood-hosted routing.

Two items to be aware of:
1) Failover semantics: When fallback is enabled, we only route to other regions inside the same jurisdiction where possible (e.g., US regions remain in US). If capacity is exhausted and strict residency is enforced, requests will be rejected rather than routed.
2) Legal transfer mechanisms: for cross-border movement of logs or analytics data we rely on contractual safeguards in our DPA and standard SCC-equivalent clauses for customers in jurisdictions that require them. We can add explicit language referencing binding corporate rules or SCCs if your legal team requests it.

If you need us to run a short ingest test from your staging app and show the request trace and region selection in the console, we can do that next week.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Amanda Chen <amanda@clearwaterhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwaterhealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency and cross-border routing questions

Thanks for the detail — very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from legal/procurement:

- Please confirm that disabling fallback will indeed prevent any automatic cross-border routing and that the system will return an explicit error when capacity is unavailable. We need this behavior documented in the DPA.
- For subprocessors that may see telemetry, can you confirm which ones have access to raw prompt text (if any)? The CSV shows LogStore Inc. — does that include raw prompt payloads or only structured logs?

Procurement also requested the DPA clause template and the DocuSign link for the standard DPA so they can start an internal review.

— Amanda

-----Original Message-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amanda Chen <amanda@clearwaterhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@clearwaterhealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency and cross-border routing questions

Amanda — quick confirmation and next steps:

1) Behavior when fallback is disabled: confirmed. If you set "Disable cross-region fallback" at the workspace level we will block routing to out-of-region compute and return an HTTP 503 with an explicit error code (RESIDENCY_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED) when capacity is unavailable. We will include that behavior in the DPA template.

2) Raw prompt access: LogStore Inc. only ingests structured operational logs (request IDs, latency metrics, error stacks). Raw prompt/response payloads are not forwarded to LogStore. AuditVault and our retention vaults are governed; raw prompts are stored only in your selected workspace region unless you opt-in to analytics replication.

3) Artifacts: attached are the Security Appendix (contains SOC2 exhibits references), the CSV subprocessors export, and a DPA clause template (Docx). DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/CLW-CWH-DPA-2026 (same as the related_links above).

Let me know if you want us to add specific language for SCCs/BCRs — Priyom and Monica can propose wording. Happy to run an ingest trace with your staging account as well.

Best regards,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
